shortDescription: The German day-ahead power contract rose to its highest level since December 2024 on Monday, ahead of an expected slump in wind power generation.($1 = 0.8714 euros)

children: The German day-ahead power contract rose to its highest level since December 2024 on Monday, ahead of an expected slump in wind power generation.
The German day-ahead baseload power contract (TRDEBD1) was up by 147.9% to €238 ($273) per megawatt hour at 0742 GMT, according to LSEG data.

"Looking ahead, German wind generation is expected to drop sharply overnight and average only around 5 GW tomorrow. Output should remain mostly low through Friday, with only a brief rebound to around 14 GW on Thursday," analysts at Engie's EnergyScan wrote.
Wind power generation in Germany was set to fall by 22 gigawatts, consumption was seen up by 1.1 GW to 54.8 GW, and solar power generation was expected to remain largely unchanged at 12.8 GW.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) was down 3.7% to €137/MWh.
Consumption in France was expected to rise by 1.3 GW to 43.9 GW, wind power generation was set to edge nearly 1 GW higher and solar power generation was seen largely stable at 5.9 GW.
French nuclear availability fell by 8 percentage points to 70% of total capacity.
State-owned electric utility EDF flagged on Friday that due to low flow rates on the Vienne river,  it might need to temporarily reduce the output of the Civaux Nuclear Power Plant from October 1.
The German 2027 baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) fell 0.4% to €131.2/MWh, LSEG data showed.
The French year-ahead contract (TRFRBYc1) was untraded.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was up 0.5% to €87.41 a metric ton.
